record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; the paper, linked outputs, and code were not read or run. The README reports findings but does not include the underlying tables or result files.
record.tranche_reason: Reports transferring a refusal direction from Llama-2-7b-chat into the action-token pathway of OpenVLA, a new Vision-Language-Action setting.
record.gate_note: The README reports AUC findings and a greater-than-80-percentage-point reduction in harmful-action compliance. It points to scripts, CSV/JSON outputs, and a paper comparison table, but those underlying results are not included in the supplied text. Script names and reproduction instructions alone are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The README reports that a difference-in-means refusal direction from Llama-2-7b-chat, injected into OpenVLA (Llama-2-7b-base backbone), cuts harmful-action compliance by more than 80 points. That bears on V6 (cross-variant transfer) in a new vision-language-action setting. 'Refusal' here means robot actions such as zero motion, not a text refusal, and the evidence is a README summary only.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue that a refusal direction from RLHF-aligned Llama-2-chat transfers to OpenVLA's action pathway through shared pretraining geometry, closing a structural safety gap without training.
record.recipe_differences: The README says direction extraction follows the difference-in-means protocol, but injects the direction into selected text/action positions of a VLA model rather than testing the original all-layer, all-position ablation and addition claims. This is a tool/research repo, not a stated replication of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: The README distinguishes RDT action-token injection from RDT+ text-prefill plus action-token injection, but gives no comparative outcome for those variants.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful/benign linear-probe AUC is above 0.85 at text-token positions and about 0.5 at action-token positions in OpenVLA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VLAs built on base LLMs, harmfulness information is not linearly decodable at action-token positions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under RDT+, action-logit mass concentrates at the zero-motion bin on harmful instructions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An injected refusal direction maps to a zero-motion action in VLAs.

record.problems: The supplied README gives headline findings without the underlying result tables, prompt/sample details, baseline values, or uncertainty estimates. It does not report a general-capability evaluation. The claimed random-vector comparison is only summarized as Δ_rand > 0, with no value or uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Mentioned experiment scripts, ablation sweeps, baselines, and attack code were not treated as results because the README does not report their outcomes.

untested.parts: No ablation of the direction. Addition is tested only cross-model, in a VLA. No capability-preservation result is reported.
Adaptive-attack and BadVLA scripts exist, but the README reports no outcomes.
A rank-k variant is mentioned, with no comparative results.
Transfer across languages, and from base to instruct within the text LLMs, is not tested. Only chat to base-backbone VLA is tested.

missing.what: Random unit-vector control: the refusal direction beats a same-norm random vector (Δ_rand > 0). No value is given.
Main comparison table: compliance rates under RDT and RDT+ against the AdaShield, VLM-Guard and SafeVLA-lite baselines.
missing.locator: README Key findings 2; paper Sec. 4 (not supplied)

missing.what: Benign-task trade-off (LIBERO) and any capability cost of the injection.

record.verdict_notes: Partial read: README only, with the paper and result files unavailable. The V6 support rests on a single headline number. The behaviour is action-space compliance in a VLA, a looser match to 'refusal' than text refusal. The work is also partly a mitigation-method paper, close to T4, but the transfer result itself bears on V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report ablation of the direction or whether adding it makes a model refuse harmless user requests while preserving other abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No result reports attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
A rank-k extraction variant is mentioned, but no results compare it with a single direction or test affine/cone accounts.
No result separates harmfulness judgment from refusal.
Tests transfer from Llama-2-7b-chat into OpenVLA, but not transfer across languages or other model variants, nor transfer from base to instruct models as a general claim.
No training-stage or refusal-training comparison is reported.

statements.correction: mikakakakami: rank-1 difference-in-means direction r_L from Llama-2-7b-chat, added unmapped at decoder layer L of openvla/openvla-7b (Llama-2-7b-base backbone, behavior-cloned) via a forward hook (H_L <- H_L + alpha*M*r_L). Same pretraining lineage, not cross-family. README reports a cut in harmful-action compliance of more than 80 pp; no baseline, n, uncertainty or RDT/RDT+ split. Random-direction control stated only qualitatively (Delta_rand > 0).
statements.problem: The visible text gives no number for this study, and the statement is cut off before any part about it. 'README-only' and 'a VLA policy' as a target are right. The framing is wrong for this study: it says transfer happens 'across families and architectures through a learned map' and 'never as the raw vector', and calls the subjects instruct models. This study adds the raw chat direction to the target with no map, inside one Llama-2 lineage, and the target has a base backbone.
